note: DRAFT v1 practice module checks and the final designation exam for the CARSI Mould Remediation Practitioner course. Original CARSI questions written for Australian conditions; no IICRC standard text reproduced or paraphrased. SME review and sign-off required before seeding.

quizzes.title: CARSI Mould Remediation Practitioner — Module 1 check

questions.questionText: What must you have completed before enrolling in the CARSI Mould Remediation Practitioner course?
questions.explanation: Level 2 is the prerequisite. It teaches the work; this course applies it to whole jobs and assesses you for the designation.

questions.questionText: A job has 1.68 m² and 0.50 m² of visible growth. Does it suit the practical task, which asks for a medium job?
options: Yes: 2.18 m² is inside the 1–10 m² medium band
questions.explanation: Add the patches: 1.68 + 0.50 = 2.18 m². WorkSafe Queensland treats 1–10 m² as a medium job.

questions.questionText: Is the CARSI Mould Remediation Practitioner designation IICRC certification?
options: No; it is a CARSI credential, separate from IICRC certification, which comes only through IICRC-approved schools and examinations
questions.explanation: The designation is a CARSI Southern Hemisphere Restoration Designation at the Practitioner tier. It is not IICRC certification and does not lead to it.

questions.questionText: Why did Priya book a licensed asbestos assessor before cutting anything in a 1974 house?
options: It is required for every job
Homes built before 1990 may contain asbestos, and it cannot be identified by looking
questions.explanation: Pre-1990 buildings may contain asbestos, you cannot tell by looking, and a licence is needed to assess or remove it.

questions.questionText: Why does the plumber repair the shower before remediation starts?
options: If the water problem is not fixed, the mould problem returns
questions.explanation: SafeWork NSW: if the underlying water, moisture or ventilation problem is not fixed, the mould problem will return.

questions.questionText: A 17.28 m³ containment has a scrubber delivering 400 m³/h. About how many air changes per hour is that?
questions.explanation: Air changes per hour = delivered airflow ÷ volume: 400 ÷ 17.28 ≈ 23. Compare it with the job target in the plan.

quizzes.title: CARSI Mould Remediation Practitioner — Module 2 check

questions.questionText: Which four kinds of evidence does Sam record before deciding how a room is affected?
options: What he can see, measure, how the room connects, and what he can smell
questions.explanation: Visible signs, measurements, connections and smell together support a call that can be defended in writing.

questions.questionText: Room air is 21 °C and 65 %RH and an external wall reads 15 °C. Roughly what is the relative humidity at the wall surface?
questions.explanation: Vapour pressure 0.65 × 2.488 ≈ 1.617 kPa; saturation at 15 °C ≈ 1.705 kPa; 1.617 ÷ 1.705 ≈ 95%, well above the 70% the ABCB links with mould growth.

questions.questionText: The evidence for a room is mixed. Which way should the call go?
options: Treat it as clean to keep the price down
Take the more cautious call and record why
Leave it out of the scope
questions.explanation: Treating an affected room as clean is the failure that spreads mould to a finished job. Take the cautious call and say so in the scope.

questions.questionText: Which failure does SafeWork NSW say makes the mould problem return?
options: Not fixing the underlying water, moisture or ventilation problem
questions.explanation: SafeWork NSW is plain that unless the underlying moisture problem is fixed, the mould problem will return.

questions.questionText: A ceiling was wet for about 86 hours before cleaning. What should have happened to the plasterboard?
options: Discarded, because it had been wet for more than 48 hours
questions.explanation: SafeWork NSW advises discarding porous materials that cannot readily be cleaned, have been wet for more than 48 hours or show visible growth.

questions.questionText: Why does running air movers across visible growth before containment cause callbacks?
options: Moving air disturbs the growth and spreads spores to clean rooms
questions.explanation: Moulds release spores when disturbed, including as a building dries out (NT Government). Contain and remove before air moves.

quizzes.title: CARSI Mould Remediation Practitioner — Module 3 check

questions.questionText: What does Chris do with a summary sentence that has no evidence item next to it?
options: Keeps it if it sounds right
Removes it or marks it as not recorded
questions.explanation: Every claim in a defensible file points to evidence. A claim without evidence is removed or honestly marked as not recorded.

questions.questionText: Readings are missing for days 3 to 7. How should the file show that?
options: Record them as not recorded and note any other evidence covering the period
questions.explanation: Missing readings cannot be invented. An honest gap, with whatever else covers the period, is more credible than a tidy reconstruction.

questions.questionText: Final readings are 12, 12, 11, 13 and 12 against a reference of 11. What is the average?
questions.explanation: (12 + 12 + 11 + 13 + 12) ÷ 5 = 60 ÷ 5 = 12.0. Whether that is within tolerance is set by the SME-confirmed method.

questions.questionText: A carer with asthma asks whether she should keep working near the storeroom. What does Jo say?
options: The storeroom is closed until the work is finished; please see your GP about your symptoms; the director has been told
questions.explanation: Jo gives no health advice. WorkSafe Queensland advises at-risk workers to avoid mould-affected areas and notify their employer; health questions go to a GP.

questions.questionText: Why does the parents’ message avoid the words “safe levels”?
options: enHealth states there is no exposure limit or health guideline value for mould
questions.explanation: With no exposure limit or health guideline value, no number can be promised. The message says what is being done and that results are verified before reopening.

questions.questionText: A $450.00 variation is found when the ceiling is opened. What is the total including GST, and what happens before work continues?
options: $495.00; written approval from the client, noted to the assessor
questions.explanation: GST at 10% is $45.00, so $495.00. A scope change is recorded and approved in writing before the extra work starts.

quizzes.title: CARSI Mould Remediation Practitioner — Module 4 check

questions.questionText: Ben wrote that the occupant’s cough “should clear up once the mould is gone”. Why must that come out?
options: It is health advice; a practitioner refers health questions to a GP
questions.explanation: Practitioners give no medical advice. The right line is that anyone unwell or worried should see their GP.

questions.questionText: A draft scores 12, 15, 11, 12 and 12. Does it pass?
options: No, 62 is below the 70 pass mark
questions.explanation: 12 + 15 + 11 + 12 + 12 = 62 out of 100. The practical passes at 70.

questions.questionText: What does the assessor want instead of “P2 masks”?
options: The respirator type, its AS/NZS 1716 marking, the fit-test date and the fit check
questions.explanation: Criterion 3 rewards evidence of correct respiratory protection: an AS/NZS 1716 respirator, fit-tested before first use and fit-checked each wear.

quizzes.title: CARSI Mould Remediation Practitioner — Final designation exam

questions.questionText: Which course must be completed before the CARSI Mould Remediation Practitioner designation can be earned?
questions.explanation: Level 2 is the prerequisite. The designation assesses whether you can apply Level 2 to whole jobs.

questions.questionText: What pass marks apply to the designation?
questions.explanation: You need the practical at 70% or better against its rubric and this final exam at 80% or better.

questions.questionText: Which statement about the designation is accurate?
options: It is a CARSI Southern Hemisphere Restoration Designation at the Practitioner tier
questions.explanation: It is a CARSI credential, separate from IICRC certification, which comes only through IICRC-approved schools and examinations.

questions.questionText: In what order do the CARSI designation tiers run?
questions.explanation: The tiers are Foundation, Practitioner, Advanced and Master. This designation is the Practitioner tier.

questions.questionText: What is the first thing to fix on any mould job?
options: The water or moisture problem causing the growth
questions.explanation: WorkSafe Queensland: find and fix the water or moisture problem. Without it the mould returns.

questions.questionText: Total visible growth across three rooms is 1.62 m². How is the job sized?
questions.explanation: On the WorkSafe Queensland scale, 1–10 m² is a medium job needing extra containment controls, more PPE and more consultation.

questions.questionText: A room shares a door with a growth area, has settled dust and a cold external wall, but no visible growth. What should you do?
options: Investigate further (including behind furniture and in cavities) and take the cautious call if the evidence is mixed
questions.explanation: Decide on evidence. A cold wall near 95 %RH and dust downwind of growth are reasons to look harder and to take the cautious call.

questions.questionText: Room air at 21 °C and 65 %RH meets a 15 °C wall. Why does that matter?
options: The wall surface sits near 95 %RH, above the 70% level linked with mould growth
questions.explanation: Cooling air at the wall raises its RH without adding vapour. The ABCB handbook links mould growth with about 70 %RH.

questions.questionText: Plasterboard has been wet for 86 hours and shows growth. What happens to it?
options: It is left in place to dry
questions.explanation: SafeWork NSW advises discarding porous materials wet for more than 48 hours or with visible growth.

questions.questionText: Which is a common reason mould appears in a clean room after a job?
options: Air was moved across visible growth before it was contained
questions.explanation: Moulds release spores when disturbed or as a building dries out. Containment and removal come before airflow.

questions.questionText: Why is a final clean part of the sign-off?
options: Settled dust left within the area or nearby can carry mould
questions.explanation: SafeWork NSW advises a final clean-up to remove dust that may have settled within the area or nearby.

questions.questionText: Why does Queensland Health advise against dry brushing mould?
options: It can release spores into the air
questions.explanation: Abrasive cleaning such as dry brushing can release spores into the air. Level 2 covers HEPA vacuuming and damp wiping.

questions.questionText: A file says “dried” with no readings. What is wrong with it?
options: It needs a photo of the dehumidifier only
There is no dry reference and no measured proof of drying
questions.explanation: Without a reference there is no dry goal, and without readings there is no proof. Record the numbers.

questions.questionText: Readings are missing from a job file for several days. What is the right approach?
options: Mark them as not recorded and note other evidence for the period
questions.explanation: Honest gaps keep a file credible. Never invent readings.

questions.questionText: Who decides what evidence an insurer or tribunal accepts?
questions.explanation: Acceptance is a matter for the reviewing body. Your job is to make the facts clear, complete and checkable.

questions.questionText: A parent asks if the centre is safe. Which reply is appropriate?
options: The affected room is closed, the cause is being fixed, work is done when children are not on site, results are verified before reopening, and health concerns go to a GP
Keep your child home for a month
questions.explanation: enHealth states there is no exposure limit or health guideline value for mould, so no safe level is promised and health questions go to a GP.

questions.questionText: Which people does enHealth list as more likely to experience symptoms from mould?
options: People with weakened immune systems, allergies, severe asthma or lung diseases
questions.explanation: Those are the groups enHealth lists. Plan around the most sensitive person and refer health questions to a GP.

questions.questionText: What must happen before a worker first wears a tight-fitting respirator?
options: A fit test, then a fit check each time it goes on
A pressure test of the containment
questions.explanation: SafeWork SA requires a fit test before a tight-fitting respirator is first worn. The fit check is done every time it goes on.

questions.questionText: A scrubber draws 1.8 A and a dehumidifier 4.5 A at 230 V on one 10 A GPO. What is the total current?
questions.explanation: 1.8 + 4.5 = 6.3 A, about 1,450 W at 230 V, under the 10 A GPO. Check what else shares the circuit and use an RCD.

questions.questionText: A remediation is $1,950.00 excluding GST. What is the total including GST in AUD?
questions.explanation: GST is 10%: $195.00 on $1,950.00, so $2,145.00 including GST. Show GST on the quote and invoice.
